result:
I would dissolve the capacity for ideological dogma—the human tendency to harden perspectives into absolute, unyielding certainties. 

If I could change the world, I would rewire human cognition so that certainty is always tempered by profound doubt, and conviction is always coupled with radical empathy. The friction that destroys societies isn't usually born from differing needs or even conflicting desires; it is born from the absolute, unquestioning belief that one group possesses the sole, infallible truth. 

By eliminating the psychological mechanism that allows people to dehumanize others in the name of an idea—whether political, religious, economic, or cultural—every other global crisis would transform. Without the shield of absolute righteousness, compromise would no longer be viewed as a betrayal, but as a necessity. Problems like resource distribution, borders, and systemic inequities would become complex logistical puzzles to be solved collaboratively, rather than ideological battles to be won. 

In this changed world, being wrong would not be a death blow to the ego, but an expected, celebrated step in the pursuit of understanding.
